content:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a bunch of gRPC streaming stalls from image-ingest pods to model-hosts in us-west-2a -> us-west-2b. Streams open fine then hang and eventually reset. ~20-30% error rate on long-lived streams. :frowning:
jonathan: Any commonalities? same node pairs / same VNIs?
maria: Looks correlated to nodes that have sidecar proxy (envoy) + ipsec tunnel for cross-AZ traffic. When path MTU hits ~1420 we see fragmentation.
lee: That sounds like PMTU + encapsulation. ESP added ~60 bytes -> egress MTU needs to be reduced. Are we clamping?
sam: I pulled a tcpdump on the server and on the pod interface. Interesting: packets > 1400 get fragmented on the wire and the gRPC stream stalls during chunked SendMessage.
maria: tcpdump (node eth0):
```
09:23:11.123456 IP 10.0.12.34.443 > 10.0.45.67.54832: Flags [P.], seq 1:16385, ack 1, win 512, length 16384
09:23:11.153000 IP (frag 1) 10.0.12.34 > 10.0.45.67: frag 0 65496 (DF)
```
jonathan: envoys usually set `do_not_fragment`? Could be DF set by userland and routers not doing PMTU ICMP blackhole.
lee: Confirmed we have DF set on kernel `ip rule` via proxy? Also noticed calico tunnel (ipip/geneve) MTU default 1450 on some nodes. Mixing encapsulations + ipsec likely pushes packets over physical MTU.
sam: From pod netns: `ip link show eth0 mtu 1500` but overlay interface on node is 1450 on some hosts. So pod thinks 1500 but path can't handle that once esp encap applied.
maria: Repro steps: 1) Start long streaming RPC from pod->pod across AZ 2) Send ~40KB frame 3) stream stalls (no ACK progress) after fragmented packets.
lee: Is this specific to gRPC or any tcp stream?
maria: Mostly shows up with gRPC streaming because it relies on many small frames and windowing; but we've seen similar TCP stalls for bulk transfers (rsync-like) on same links.
jonathan: Any RDMA nodes involved? Those might bypass the stack and behave differently.
sam: Affected nodes are mixed — some have Mellanox RNICs with SR-IOV; weirdly the RNIC hosts show fewer stalls (maybe offload handles reassembly differently).
lee: Quick mitigation: clamp MSS on the egress iptables mangle for pod traffic to 1300. That stops the fragmentation.
maria: Can we push ClusterConfig change to set calico/geneve MTU to 1400 and make CNI advertise it to pods? That would be less hacky than iptables on every node.
jonathan: We should also enable path-mtu-discovery ICMP allowed on the egress ACLs — currently our firewall drops ICMP unreachable which means PMTU never adjusts.
sam: I pushed a canary rule on one node group: `iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` — results: stream success in canary.
lee: Nice. But long-term we should: set CNI MTU to (physical_mtu - max_encap_overhead), enable MSS clamp on host networking layer for any encapsulation, and unblock ICMP PTB.
maria: Filed infra ticket https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1287 to track: audit encap types per AZ, set cluster MTU policy, and rollout MSS clamp via daemonset for edge.
infra-bot: Deploy report: canary iptables-mss-clamp applied to 3 nodes in us-west-2b at 2026-03-17T09:55:00Z. Health checks passed.
sre-oncall: For oncall: if you see gRPC stream stall alerts, check `ss -tanm` and look for retransmits + `ip -s link` for rx/tx errors. Also check `sudo tc -s qdisc show dev <iface>` for queuing.
jonathan: Also add a monitoring metric: percent of streams experiencing retransmission > 5% per nodepair. If it spikes, auto-apply MSS clamp to that nodepair.
maria: Will follow up with a short runbook. For now canary looks good, rolling to all us-west nodes after config review. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
